speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, scammers use AI and information about us online, among other capabilities, to make themselves more believable and evade easy detection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fundamentally, these scams are successful because they prey on universal human emotions, such as a desire for companionship, respect for authority, and greed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In some cases, the victims are so convinced by the scammers that they refuse to believe that they are being scammed, despite being repeatedly advised by their loved ones and the Police.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It shows how far the Government is going to tackle the issue of scams involving self-effected transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It will only be used as a last resort, after all efforts to convince the individual have failed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are glad that most members of the public understand this and support it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is working with banks to introduce cooling-off periods for high-risk transactions, such as requests to increase transaction limits or to change contact details.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These cooling-off periods provide a cognitive break for individuals and give them an opportunity to reassess their actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The cooling-off period also gives authorities more time to detect if something suspicious is taking place and to stop any scam transactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These moves build on the suite of anti-scam measures which MAS has been working with the banks to put in place over the years, such as Money Lock, Kill-Switch and enhanced fraud surveillance to alert victims and block scam transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Collectively, they underscore the critical role that banks play in our fight against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to proactively strengthen our defences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One priority is to improve the authentication methods that banks use to protect accounts against malware and phishing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since July 2024, the major retail banks in Singapore have progressively phased out the use of SMS One-Time Password (OTP) for account logins by customers who have digital tokens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also studying stronger authentication solutions, such as the use of Fast IDentity Online-compliant hardware tokens, otherwise known as FIDO, which need to be in close proximity to the user's device to authenticate the transaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will fortify our defences against malware and phishing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we have strengthened our protection of bank accounts, scammers have pivoted their playbook.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They have started asking victims to convert their money to cryptocurrencies prior to performing the transfers, thereby evading our banking safeguards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They have also targeted assets stored in victims' crypto wallets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members will know that cryptocurrency is largely unregulated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Singapore, MAS has licensed a number of digital payment token service providers with certain regulatory safeguards in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with these digital payment token service providers to strengthen anti-scam controls and tighten operational links with law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But there are many other online exchanges and wallet providers which are not regulated and they are outside the reach of our laws because they operate from overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Furthermore, the anonymity features of certain cryptocurrency transactions can be exploited by criminals to evade capture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MAS has repeatedly cautioned retail investors against investing in cryptocurrencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And I want to repeat this appeal today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I know some people are attracted because they think crypto is an opportunity for them to make a quick buck.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They think that so long as they do their own research, they understand the risks, they would not lose money and they would not get scammed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: My dear fellow Singaporeans, even crypto-savvy individuals have lost badly by trading in crypto when their values plummet or when they fall prey to scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These sophisticated criminal syndicates are going after both crypto-novice and crypto-savvy investors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They invest in elaborate fake crypto trading interfaces to scam you into thinking that you are profiting from your crypto investments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some embed malware or phishing links to drain your crypto wallets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, we have seen meme coin prices soar rapidly before crashing in pump-and-dump schemes, leaving consumers with significant losses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, our advice to the general public is to steer clear of cryptocurrencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The risk of getting burnt is high and, should you fall victim to a scam, the chances of you getting even a single dollar back is very low.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another common scam modality is scam calls and SMSes, which many of us are familiar with.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: About 20% of scam cases in 2024 involved victims being contacted in this way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been working to suppress scam calls and SMSes for some time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Telcos have allowed subscribers to block calls from international numbers and have pre-emptively blocked international calls with spoofed +65 prefixes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But scammers have pivoted to using local phone numbers to try to catch people unawares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is why we have been taking measures to tighten the ownership and abuse of local SIM cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, to strengthen accountability for SIM cards, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) limited the number of post-paid SIM cards that a person can own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From 1 January this year, the Police have operationalised offences, including registering for a SIM card and then selling it for a gain, possessing a large number of unregistered SIM cards for no legitimate reason, and buying or selling SIM cards registered in another person's particulars.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We take a very serious view of anyone who assists scam operations in this way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will not hesitate to use the full range of these penalties against people who abuse SIM cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is the same approach we have taken for money mules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been clamping down on them, because they are the main way that overseas scammers launder their ill-gotten gains and transfer monies out of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More than 660 have been charged in Court and they face imprisonment if found guilty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In one concluded case, a money mule received RM$1,000 for sharing access to his Internet banking account with another person, without taking reasonable steps to ascertain the purpose of this arrangement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The money mule was convicted and sentenced to six months' imprisonment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked if there is more we can do to better detect money mule activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For 2025, we will be expanding our efforts on this front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF will expand information sharing with the banks on known mule accounts, to enhance banks' fraud analytics and enable banks to uncover other mule accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also work with the industry to implement cooling-off measures for certain activities which are tell-tale signs of money mule activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To those who think that they can make an easy profit by passing on their SIM cards or bank accounts to strangers and turning a blind eye to what they are used for, let me be very clear.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a crime and there is an imprisonment term for passing on your SIM cards or your bank accounts to facilitate scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Claiming ignorance does not get you off the hook.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Dr Tan Wu Meng asked if the penalties for scam-related offences are still too soft, with Dr Tan suggesting that caning should be legislated for egregious offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Mr Nair and Dr Tan that we need stiff and deterrent sentences against those who facilitate scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Sentencing Advisory Panel (SAP) has recently proposed significant imprisonment terms for offences which facilitate scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will consider Dr Tan's suggestion for caning to be prescribed for certain scam-related offences, recognising the serious harm they can cause.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will do what we can to deter and disrupt scam activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But at the end of the day, persistent scammers will find a way to reach Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, what Singaporeans want to know is: how can I protect myself?

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Mr Derrick Goh all had ideas on how we can better educate the public to deal with scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are useful suggestions and we will consider them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: My advice to Singaporeans is to use the ScamShield Suite, which was launched in September last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It comprises the ScamShield app, a helpline, website, as well as WhatsApp and Telegram alert channels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The public can use these various channels to easily, one, check if something is a scam; two, report scams; and three, stay updated on scam trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If you are unsure if something is a scam, or you think you are being scammed and want to know what to do, call 1799 which is the ScamShield hotline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, we will alert Singaporeans to high-loss scam types through monthly media campaigns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These campaigns are tailored to the population segments which are most vulnerable to each scam type.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There is one critical area which we can do better in and, that is, our online space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We can and we must do much more to prevent such scams from happening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Derrick Goh and Assoc Prof Razwana pointed out, achieving this will require close collaboration with tech companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the Government's part, we have put in place two Codes of Practice under the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA), the Online Communication Code and E-Commerce Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These require designated online services, such as messaging apps, social media platforms and e-commerce platforms to implement measures to proactively prevent and disrupt scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Keith Chua and Mdm Mariam Jaafar asked if messaging apps and social media platforms have been cooperative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They have generally been responsive to the legal requirements under OCHA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, as part of the E-commerce Code, Meta has implemented enhanced verification against Government-issued records for select sellers on Facebook Marketplace and advertisers on Facebook.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Carousell has done the same for risky sellers on its platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This has made it more difficult for scammers to exploit these platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We thank Meta and Carousell for working with the Government on this and protecting users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The success of these efforts underscores a simple but powerful truth: robust user verification by online platforms deters online crime as criminals know that they cannot hide behind the cloak of anonymity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We strongly encourage all online platforms, including social media platforms and messaging apps, to put in place robust user verification measures, in particular, checking against Government-issued identity documents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Email addresses and phone numbers are no longer sufficient as verification methods, as they are prone to abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One platform we are especially concerned about is Telegram, which has long prioritised, and even prided itself in, the anonymity that it provides its users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This anonymity is exploited by scammers and other criminals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Sexually explicit non-consensual videos are being circulated on Telegram.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We urge Telegram to take the online safety of its users seriously and adopt stronger user verification measures to prevent scammers from creating scam accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MHA is monitoring the situation closely and we will explore further measures to address the scam situation on Telegram, including making use of our legislative levers to ensure compliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That aside, we continue to track the worrying trend of Government official impersonation scams, including on social media accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been engaging social media platforms to remove these, including through OCHA take-down directions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But as Mdm Jaafar has highlighted, these scams still persist.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our view is that social media companies can do more to put in place preventive measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are studying potential regulatory levers to better safeguard our online space on this front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, we will double down on our efforts to developed AI tech solutions to deal with scams that can be pushed out at speed and scale, as Mr Derrick Goh has pointed out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have co-developed the Scam Analytics and Tactical Intervention System (SATIS) suite of products, which leverages artificial intelligence and machine learning to help the Police detect, assess and disrupt scam websites and accounts swiftly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are expanding SATIS to disrupt other scam enablers, such as payment channels and mobile numbers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Thus far, I have spoken about the steps we will take to strengthen our defences here in Singapore against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Vikram Nair and Assoc Prof Razwana have asked how we can better act against scam operators outside of Singapore and improve asset recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singapore works closely with foreign law enforcement agencies on joint operations against scam syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, SPF participated in INTERPOL's Operation HAECHI V last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In terms of crypto assets, more than $798,000 were seized, arising from the blocking of more than 1,000 crypto accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Apart from working through INTERPOL, we have also conducted operations directly with other countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Asset recovery is also a priority for us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to conclude this segment of my speech with some comments in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Last year, investment scams, job scams and Government official impersonation scams were the three types of scams that caused the most significant losses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These scams succeeded primarily because scammers prey on human vulnerabilities, such as the desire for companionship, respect for authority and greed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some victims are so convinced by the scammers that they refuse to believe that they are being deceived, even after repeated warnings from family members and the Police.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Additionally, we have worked with banks to implement a “cooling off” period for high-risk transactions, such as the raising transaction limits and changing contact information, giving people an opportunity to pause, reflect and reassess their decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This also gives the authorities more time to identify suspicious activities and prevent fraudulent transactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an additional measure to protect bank deposits beyond our basic existing protective measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These basic measures include the Money Lock, Kill-Switch features and the fraud monitoring system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This can promptly alert scam victims and stop fraudulent transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, we are taking strict actions against criminals who misuse local SIM cards for scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They try to evade the law by claiming that they are unaware of how their SIMs were used, but this excuse will not absolve them of responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: People should use existing resources to protect themselves, such as the Money Lock feature, and protect their bank deposits and obtaining anti-scam information through ScamShield.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When in doubt, they can also call ScamShield hotline 1799.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let us all work together to prevent scams, protect ourselves and care for our family members. : Let me now address the queries that Members have raised on matters beyond scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about additional safeguards in the law to better protect healthcare workers in the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) and other mental health facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have reviewed this over the years to strengthen our laws on this front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I understand that the Police and IMH are in discussions to better coordinate responses to such incidents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, MOH is working with our public health institutions to put in place measures to safeguard our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked for an update on our efforts to level up the security industry to become more productive and less manpower-intensive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A critical enabler for this is Outcome-Based Contracting (OBC), which allows and incentivises security agencies to innovate and adopt more productive solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government has been taking the lead in OBC since May 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As of 2024, I am pleased to note that all Government procuring entities have either adopted or called tender for at least one OBC at the agency level.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope this will encourage more of the private sector to follow suit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will complement other measures, such as subsidising the adoption of technology solutions and raising the competencies of the security agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Alex Yam asked about the threats to racial and religious harmony in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As a small, open and globally connected country, we are vulnerable to external influence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Religious extremism and far-right extremist ideologies have inspired some Singaporeans to consider violence and even plan attacks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Foreign events also have the potential to arouse local sentiments and polarise our society along racial and religious lines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why we agree with Mr Zhulkarnain and Mr Alex Yam that countering such threats requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We collaborate with our community partners, which include religious organisations, schools and hospitals, to enhance our ability to prevent, detect and respond to terror attacks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond community engagement, our laws and policies protect our common civic space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We cannot legislate people to get along or integrate with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Maintaining our social stability and cohesiveness will require our collective effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is about how each of us conducts ourselves in the common space, whether we take the trouble to appreciate and celebrate one another’s differences and recognise the value that we each bring to our society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I have two sets of clarifications for Minister Josephine Teo and Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, what steps are being taken to raise this awareness?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, on the Re-integration Hub initiative – full disclosure – I am a member of the Yellow Ribbon Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I love the work of the Re-integration Hub.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And what kind of a response have we been getting from external stakeholders when they contribute to this cause?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Zhulkarnain for his very important questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Perhaps, I will take the third one first, in which he correctly pointed out that even as we are using technology more to support our operations, we need to help the public understand how these technologies are deployed in support of our efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think we have been fortunate in the sense that when we rolled out the network of closed-circuit television (CCTVs), or what is referred to as PolCams in general, we saw a very positive response in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, if we were to ask people whether they see the usefulness of this CCTV network in detecting and solving crimes, the response level will be very positive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would say that if we take the question further and ask people what contributes to them feeling safe when they go out at night, for example, the top reason cited is often, again, the CCTVs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we have a situation where Singaporeans became sensitised to the usefulness of technology, and they saw it being deployed in a very tangible way and helping them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, building on that sort of foundation, what Home Team agencies have done consistently is that whenever they have opportunities, they have events where there are public touchpoints, they will introduce the technologies that are being used.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have attended the workplan presentations of SCDF, as well as ICA, for example, where these technologies are exhibited.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Media is invited to cover the events and, through the media, we get the word out on what is being used to carry out the Home Team's missions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to do so and find every possible opportunity to introduce the kinds of technologies that are being deployed in support of law enforcement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Perhaps, turning to the Member's two questions that are related to how SCDF seeks to strengthen its local core, as well as to ensure that its foreign hires are able to carry out its mission, first, let me deal with the strategies that we have put in place to ensure that SCDF careers remain attractive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, we have also regularly reviewed our salaries and these efforts are to ensure that SCDF careers remain attractive to locals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the Member's second question, let me, first, say that we will always try and open up recruitment pathways and be willing to consider people of more varied backgrounds, as well as train them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our preference, of course, is always to recruit and train locals but, as Mr Zhulkarnain has alluded to, we must also balance this against the growing needs, because if we are not able to bring relief to the pressures that are faced by our officers, then, clearly, it could also compromise our ability to retain them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, being able to supplement this with some foreign hires and to make sure that we are able to meet all of Singapore's needs, that is an avenue of support that we have gone towards as well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Now, let me assure Members of the training requirements that the foreign hires must meet.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, they have to go through bridging and onboarding courses, and they will, even before they are deployed, be put on on-the-job ambulance attachments with local senior paramedics to ensure that they are well-assimilated and equipped to operate in line with SCDF's professional standards and protocols.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The foreign hires will all be required to pass English language requirements to ensure that they can communicate clearly and effectively with patients and their families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Upon deployment, the foreign hires will undergo certification tests annually, and continuous education as well as training will also be provided to them so that they can continue to fulfil the same requirements as the local hires.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, these are the suite of measures that we have put in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is located at a centralised place at Institution S2.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what we do is that we work with several partners looking at the needs of the desistors and also how they can help themselves when they are released.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These areas include employment-related, skills-related areas as well, such as financial literacy and then also religious organisations and we also work with the community partners relating to family.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Like what I shared earlier, we have the Family Engagement Model that we are piloting and then we are working with many more partners today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But of course, we have the very basic programme that we work with the community, which is the Yellow Ribbon Community Project, which continues to bring in more support, and we have many more volunteers in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, the external stakeholders have found that centralised location facility to be useful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They go to one place and they are able to reach out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the Prison Service, it is something that we find very heartening to see many partners coming on board and then, from here, we will be able to strengthen the ecosystem, all with the intention to help them to desist from offending and build up their lives again.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The first pertains to the online feedback portal on road users that the Minister of State referred to.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It states on the site, and I quote: "that it receives a large number of reports" and therefore, the Traffic Police will not provide any updates on its findings, unless the feedback provider is required to testify in Court.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just informing a feedback provider that the feedback has been received, enforcement action has been taken, or there is insufficient evidence, does not seem to be too much of a requirement on the end of the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because that feedback provider has taken the effort to download the video from ostensibly their recording devices and submitted that information to the authorities through the portal.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Perhaps there is a policy reason which we are unware of or the public is unaware of as to why the TP cannot provide an update to the feedback provider.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think it would be helpful and would encourage greater civic consciousness.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second point pertains to the blinking amber light suggestion that I give.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of the Ministry of Transport's position last week in Parliament that banning the transport of foreign workers by lorries is not practical, in my view, there should be a stronger and renewed focus on ensuring their safe transport instead.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And in that context, I hope MHA can reconsider my proposal more narrowly to incentivise the reporting of the unsafe transport of foreign workers as a pilot.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And if there are indeed excessive, exaggerated fake reports then the pilot can be reviewed accordingly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And if the pilot is successful, then perhaps it can be expanded more generally to the most vulnerable of our road users and reporting unsafe road behaviour against them, specifically elderly pedestrians and motorcyclists.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the second supplementary question, as I shared in my answer, we have the current levers which we feel are more effective in managing speeding and some of these aspects of enforcement actions that we are undertaking.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we still feel that having speed cameras and also, our different aspects of reporting that are in place will help us to manage the traffic situation better today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And with regard to the first supplementary question, we feel that the current setting is sufficiently available to the community in making or contributing to this effort of reporting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The majority of people who report do not ask what happened or the actions being undertaken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we feel that this is a good balance, whereby what is key is about how we can play a part and getting the community to work with us to see how we can report such offences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I want to assure the Member that the TP will do their best to look through all the evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Today, when we have certain things happening, we not only get evidence from one road user, we sometimes get thousands of reports and the eyeballs there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In some instances, where many people are able to see, they use our system to share the incidents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, we will continue to monitor the situation and how we can better navigate this to enhance community participation.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And hopefully, we get updates in due course.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The other clarification is for Minister of State Faishal.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: He mentioned earlier about the volunteer impact training organised by the Prison Service, called IMPACT.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Can we have more details about this new structured volunteer training framework?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It introduces structured and tiered training pathways for various volunteer schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In Prisons' work, we have quite a few schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are enhancing it in such a way that it is easier for us to provide training and also enhance the capability of our volunteers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to that, we have existing volunteers who we feel that many would benefit from a refresher course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And many of them have been with us for decades, where they have come forward to share and to really support the inmates, the ex-offenders and their families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, with IMPACT, we are introducing e-refresher courses, where they are able to get themselves updated with new trends, some of the aspects where it will help them to understand the landscape better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And with IMPACT, we are able to provide more training spaces.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is something that we feel will enhance the rehabilitation and re-integration journey of our inmates, our ex-offenders, and also help with supporting the families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The key thing about work in the prison ecosystem is that quite a big chunk of work is being supported by the community, so it is in the interest of the society, including the inmates, their families and Singapore that we enhance the capability so that they can do their role well, and support and provide the opportunities for our ex-offenders or desistors to build up their lives.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: My clarification is for Minister of State Sun.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Specifically, the Minister of State highlighted that there were scams from Telegram and also other social media platforms, including Facebook, and Carousell has been used for scams.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: There is an online Code of Conduct that they have complied with, which has reduced the scams somewhat.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Would the Ministry also consider potential legislation to require these platforms to address scams and potentially also have mechanisms for compensation of victims, if a platform is used to facilitate scams and they do not take adequate actions to prevent those scams?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: What they do, in the instance of online communication services is that they would specify what the platform should do, in the case of quick disruption of malicious accounts, for instance; or the deployment of safeguards, such as reasonable verification measures to prevent the creation and use of inauthentic accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the case of the e-commerce code, I had also mentioned in my main reply that they have recommendations in the sense of subjecting users who advertise or post about the sales of the goods and services, for them to verify against Government-issued records, as well as to provide an option for users when it comes to payment protection mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These Codes of Practice are actually quite new, since June 2024, last year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And so, right now, between MDDI as well as MHA, we are working with the social media platforms and e-commerce players for them to implement these Codes of Practice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we have seen improvements and we are trying to work off that base to expand the pilot to more categories of sellers who post their products and services online, and also, to see whether or not we can work with these platforms to increase the thresholds in what we mark as success – because I had talked about 10% and 60%.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We see whether we can push those success rates higher.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But right now, what we are doing is that we are working on a good faith basis with these platforms, to tell them that we think that the measures that we have shared thus far – whether or not it is user verification, or whether or not it is in terms of the takedown timing, and so on and so forth – that these are the targets that we are aiming for, and please comply with these recommendations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If after this initial bout of working collaboratively with them, we see that there is no desire to work collaboratively with us, then I think we have to push what we can do with them one notch further.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But right now, we are engaging with them when it comes to these Codes of Practice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are not the only country that faces issues with working with Telegram.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And this is not just in the case of scams, but also when it comes to the sale of drugs, the proliferation of sexually explicit non-consensual content online – I think we will have to consider all these harms that are prevalent on the Telegram channel.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Ms He Ting Ru, I am sorry, we have run out of time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, I am going to invite Mr Zulkarnain Abdul Rahim, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: On behalf of my fellow Parliamentarians as well, I extend our deepest gratitude to our MHA officers, men and women of the Home Team, and staff and Public Service officers, for their dedication and sacrifice in protecting our nation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: With that, Sir, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
